raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
> Note: the first commit on this branch is the EAGLE verify-append hotfix from #44199 (watermarked EAGLE/EAGLE3 output is undetectable on main without it). This branch will be rebased to a single commit once #44199 lands.

DSPARK verifies a linear draft chain. Each verify row's context is the committed watermark tail followed by the earlier draft tokens, so the existing speculative selector applies with a lower-triangular chain mask. The DSPARK worker forces those rows before acceptance. After acceptance it records the accepted rows' contexts and appends the committed tokens to the ring.

**Design: verify-side forcing.**
- A forced row's target distribution is one-hot, so DSPARK's rejection-sampling accept — with or without block verification — emits exactly the watermarked token.
- Detection therefore follows the unchanged contract: no DSPARK-specific detector logic, single and dual key alike.
- Draft-side keyed sampling would raise acceptance, but it needs the selector inside DSPARK's folded draft graph and a cropped-vocabulary hash contract. It is left as follow-up given the measured cost below.

**Evidence** (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, 8×H200, TP8/EP8, DSPARK block size 5):
- Detection: 40 essays × 512 tokens, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95. DSPARK median request z is 2.73 (16/40 at p < 1e-3) against 3.06 (18/40) without speculation on the same prompts; wrong key z 0.91. OFF: median z 0.21, 0/40.
- GSM8K-100 (temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95): 99% with 100% stop rate, both watermarked and not, 0 truncated, 0 errors.
- Throughput: bench_serving random 1024/512, c8, 100 prompts, temperature 0.8, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, six reps over two launches: TPOT +3.73%, output throughput −2.25%, accept length −3.27%.

**Also fixes** an EAGLE/NEXTN regression (#44199): the fused verify-commit path (#41175) skipped the watermark ring append, so watermarked EAGLE3 output on main is undetectable. On Qwen3-8B with EAGLE3 3/1/4, 0/40 requests reach p < 1e-3 before the fix and 40/40 after; tree 5/8/32 is also 40/40.

**Tests:**
- CUDA watermark selector/state suites, plus a DSPARK chain case. The case checks that rejection-sampling accept, with and without block verification, emits the forced tokens, and that the committed ring and context history equal those of non-speculative decode (22 passed total).
- Endpoint e2e `test_watermark.py` (5 passed).

Not covered: DSPARK with DP attention or PD disaggregation (PD stays rejected by validation). DFLASH stays rejected; its chain can reuse `force_speculative_chain` in a later PR.

nodes.body:
Yes, that's right — `_force_watermark` rewrites the selected rows of `logits_output.next_token_logits` to one-hot in place:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c3918da13e36c6704c4346010584f194ee7f08c4/python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py#L1364-L1392

That's intentional: the accept step needs to see the forced distribution, and the same tensor goes straight into `accept_and_finalize`:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c3918da13e36c6704c4346010584f194ee7f08c4/python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py#L1230-L1245

One exception: when `return_logprob` is set we force a clone instead, so `compute_spec_logprobs` still reads the pre-watermark distribution — same trick as the normal decode path in `model_runner.py`:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c3918da13e36c6704c4346010584f194ee7f08c4/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py#L2139-L2140

The L1308 `commit_hidden` you're asking about doesn't touch logits at all — it works on hidden states (`hidden_strided` / the shared aux output):

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c3918da13e36c6704c4346010584f194ee7f08c4/python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py#L1306-L1316

The selector never writes to hidden states, so the state committed for the next draft round is identical with or without the watermark. The only other readers of the forced tensor are the mask capture (L1263) and the verify observers (L1318), both of which are fine seeing the post-watermark distribution.

@@ -384,6 +385,16 @@ On a 2x GB300 node with public `Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B`, TP2, NEXTN 3/1/4, concurrency
 
 Each speculative row still requires keyed selection, but tree-context reconstruction, repeated-context admission, accepted-context recording, and ring-buffer append run as fused GPU operations. The reported cost remains workload- and acceptance-dependent.
 
+On an 8x H200 node with public `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash`, TP8 and EP8, DSPARK with `--speculative-dspark-block-size 5`, concurrency 8, 1,024-token random inputs, 512-token outputs, temperature 0.8, top-p 0.95, and top-k 20, watermarked and unwatermarked requests on the same server measured the following means over six repetitions from two server launches:
+
+| Watermark | Mean TPOT | Aggregate output throughput | Mean accept length |
+| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
+| Off | 5.879 ms | 1,226.0 token/s | 4.420 |
+| On | 6.098 ms | 1,198.4 token/s | 4.276 |
+| Change | +3.73% | -2.25% | -3.27% |
+
+A sampled DSPARK draft token is accepted on a forced row only when it equals the watermarked token, so the accept-length change depends on how closely the draft distribution tracks the target.
+
 ## See also
 
 The fused Triton selector is adapted from Meta's Apache-2.0 [TextSeal](https://github.com/facebookresearch/textseal) implementation and re-implemented on the hash contract above, so detection follows this page rather than TextSeal's own tooling.

@@ -65,7 +65,7 @@ The [operator guide's detector specification](../../../../../docs/docs/advanced_
 - **Repeated-context masking.** A context hash is forced at most once per request. Repeated contexts use ordinary sampling, preventing a deterministic short cycle from repeatedly excluding EOS. Only forced contexts enter the history.
 - **Greedy bypass.** Rows normalized to `top_k <= 1`, including `temperature=0`, use ordinary greedy selection and are not recorded.
 - **Entropy gate.** A row uses ordinary sampling when its largest truncated probability exceeds the server's `max_probability`. Skipped contexts remain eligible for a later higher-entropy occurrence.
-- **Speculative decoding.** NGRAM, EAGLE, EAGLE3, and NEXTN reconstruct verify-row contexts from the committed ring tail, tree mask, draft tokens, and positions. Normal decode preserves a clone for logprobs while speculative decode forces a clone, so both report the pre-watermark target distribution. Fused kernels admit contexts and append only accepted tokens.
+- **Speculative decoding.** NGRAM, EAGLE, EAGLE3, NEXTN, and DSPARK reconstruct verify-row contexts from the committed ring tail, tree mask, draft tokens, and positions. DSPARK verifies a linear chain, so its rows use a lower-triangular mask, and its rejection-sampling accept emits the forced token on every forced row. Normal decode preserves a clone for logprobs while speculative decode forces a clone, so both report the pre-watermark target distribution. Fused kernels admit contexts and append only accepted tokens.
 - **Selector paths.** Finite `top_k <= 8,192` uses `torch.topk`, canonicalizes boundary ties, and performs small-k truncation. Unlimited top-k retains full-vocabulary sorting. Both paths use the same hash and selection contract.
 - **Disabled-batch exit.** A host-side candidate bit follows filtering and merging. Fully disabled or greedy-only batches skip prompt initialization, verify cloning, selector work, and append kernels.
 - **Retraction and slot reuse.** Re-prefill rebuilds the distinct-context history from accepted output. A new request resets all state for a reused request-pool slot.

+    target_logits = logits.clone()
+    context_hashes, selected = state.force_speculative_chain(
+        logits=target_logits,
+        req_pool_indices=req_pool_indices,
+        chain_tokens=chain_tokens,
+        positions=torch.arange(4, device="cuda").view(1, 4),
+        sampling_info=sampling_info,
+    )
+    draft_probs = torch.softmax(
+        torch.randn(
+            (1, 3, vocab_size),
+            generator=torch.Generator("cuda").manual_seed(5),
+            device="cuda",
+        ),
+        dim=-1,
+    )
+    correct_len, bonus, _ = AcceptSampling.execute(
+        candidates=chain_tokens,
+        target_logits=target_logits,
+        draft_probs=draft_probs,
+        sampling_info=sampling_info,
+        draft_input=SimpleNamespace(max_top_k=None, uniform_top_k_value=None),
+        gamma=3,
+        verify_num_draft_tokens=4,
+        block_verification=block_verification,
+    )
+    assert correct_len.tolist() == [1]
+    assert bonus.tolist() == [forced[1]]
+
+    state.commit_speculative_chain(
+        req_pool_indices=req_pool_indices,
+        context_hashes=context_hashes,
+        selected=selected,
+        accept_tokens=torch.tensor(
+            [[forced[0], forced[1], 0, 0]], dtype=torch.int64, device="cuda"
+        ),
+        accept_lens=torch.tensor([2], dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda"),
+    )
+    assert torch.equal(
+        state.contexts_tail(req_pool_indices)[0],
+        reference.contexts_tail(req_pool_indices)[0],
+    )
+    assert state.num_watermarked_contexts.tolist() == [2]
+    assert torch.equal(
+        state.watermarked_context_hashes[0, :2],
+        reference.watermarked_context_hashes[0, :2],
+    )
+
+
 if __name__ == "__main__":
     sys.exit(pytest.main([__file__]))

inline_comments.body:
Yes, that's right — `_force_watermark` rewrites the selected rows of `logits_output.next_token_logits` to one-hot in place:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c3918da13e36c6704c4346010584f194ee7f08c4/python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py#L1364-L1392

That's intentional: the accept step needs to see the forced distribution, and the same tensor goes straight into `accept_and_finalize`:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c3918da13e36c6704c4346010584f194ee7f08c4/python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py#L1230-L1245

One exception: when `return_logprob` is set we force a clone instead, so `compute_spec_logprobs` still reads the pre-watermark distribution — same trick as the normal decode path in `model_runner.py`:

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c3918da13e36c6704c4346010584f194ee7f08c4/python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py#L2139-L2140

The L1308 `commit_hidden` you're asking about doesn't touch logits at all — it works on hidden states (`hidden_strided` / the shared aux output):

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c3918da13e36c6704c4346010584f194ee7f08c4/python/sglang/srt/speculative/dspark_components/dspark_worker_v2.py#L1306-L1316

The selector never writes to hidden states, so the state committed for the next draft round is identical with or without the watermark. The only other readers of the forced tensor are the mask capture (L1263) and the verify observers (L1318), both of which are fine seeing the post-watermark distribution.
